claim: For every infinite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space \(H\) and every nonzero Banach space \(X\), there is a sequence of rank-one operators \(R_n\in S_{\mathcal K(H,X)}\) such that \(\sup\{\inf_{n\ge1}\|S+R_n\|:S\in\mathcal K(H,X),\ \|S\|\le1\}=\sqrt{2}\). Thus this fixed countable family witnesses failure of \(\omega_1\)-octahedrality of \(\mathcal K(H,X)\) with exact gap \(2-\sqrt{2}\).

correctness.rationale: For each compact \(S\), weak nullity of the orthonormal sequence gives \(\|Se_n\|\to0\). Orthogonal decomposition \(x=a e_n+u\) and Cauchy--Schwarz yield \(\|S+R_n\|\le\sqrt{\|z+Se_n\|^2+\|S\|^2}\), hence \(\inf_n\|S+R_n\|\le\sqrt2\). The rank-one compact \(S_0=f_0\otimes z\) attains \(\sqrt2\) for every \(n\), proving equality. All quantifiers include every compact \(S\) with norm at most one.

evidence: The exact bound is uniform over every nonzero Banach target \(X\) and every compact \(S\) with \(\|S\|\le1\).
The qualitative prior result covers more general uniformly convex domains but does not provide this Hilbertian constant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The claim narrows the domain class to Hilbert spaces but strengthens the quantitative conclusion to an exact minimax value, with a matching compact rank-one extremizer.
